lead.headline: Anthropic raises $81.3bn in the biggest stock market listing ever, valuing the Claude maker at $1.5 trillion
lead.short: Anthropic raised $81.3bn in the largest initial public offering in history, pricing its shares at $83 each and valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion, the world's 12th-biggest, just behind Tesla. Investors sought six times as many shares as were on offer. Its shares start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

why.text: The listing tests how much public investors will pay for AI, at a price about 55% above the private valuation of only six months ago.

more: Anthropic sold 980 million shares, up from the 825 million it had planned, above its expected range of $70 to $78. Five years ago it raised $124m from its first investors. In May it raised $65bn privately at a $965bn valuation. It was founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including Dario and Daniela Amodei.

Its revenue reached $33.2bn in the first nine months of 2026, including $17bn in the third quarter, and it makes most of its money selling businesses access to its Claude models. Its prospectus also reported a net loss of $104bn over the first nine months of the year, as it spends heavily on computing.

update.new: The shares are priced and the record is set.
update.front: Anthropic has priced its listing at $83 a share, a record $81.3bn raised.

seconds.headline: Four are killed and Yunus's family home is set on fire in Bangladesh, as police arrest 565 before an Awami League lockdown
seconds.short: Four people were killed in clashes and the ancestral home of Muhammad Yunus, who led Bangladesh's interim government, was set on fire in Chattogram on Thursday, ahead of a nationwide lockdown called by the banned Awami League. Crude bombs went off in Dhaka before dawn, and police there arrested 565 people in a 24-hour crackdown.

why.text: The violence comes as exiled former prime minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return from India, which shelters her.

more: Those detained include former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid. Arsonists also attacked branches of Yunus's Grameen Bank in Sylhet, Rajshahi, Barishal and Faridpur. Over the past two days crude bombs were set off and vehicles torched in 28 of the country's 64 districts, and two local leaders of the ruling BNP were killed in Narail when Awami League activists attacked a march.

Prime Minister Rahman told parliament on Tuesday that the Awami League was a "terrorist outfit" and a "fallen, defeated, and ousted fascist force". Home minister Salahuddin Ahmed promised stern action. Yunus's interim government had disbanded the party and jailed thousands of its members after Hasina's fall.

seconds.headline: Henry Nicholls's unbeaten 113 lifts New Zealand to 243 for five on the first day in Wellington, with Siraj left out
seconds.short: Henry Nicholls made an unbeaten 113 off 221 balls, his 12th Test century and first against India, to take New Zealand from 12 for two to 243 for five on the first day of the first Test at the Basin Reserve. He was dropped on 102 by Devdutt Padikkal at short leg. Captain Tom Latham fell in the first over.

why.text: India left out their most successful Test bowlers of this cycle on a green pitch, and a big first-innings total would put that choice under pressure.

more: Shubman Gill picked four fast bowlers, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep, leaving out Mohammed Siraj, who has 144 wickets in 48 Tests. Ravindra Jadeja, the world's second-ranked Test all-rounder, was dropped for Washington Sundar. Siraj and Jadeja are India's top two wicket-takers in this World Test Championship cycle, with 43 and 33.

It is the first Test Siraj has missed since Pune in October 2024. Nicholls, 35, played late and scored heavily through mid-wicket while his partners fell to loose shots. "Management picked the best possible XI," said India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak. The second Test is in Christchurch from 27 November.

update.front: New Zealand made 243 for five on the first day, and India dropped Siraj and Jadeja.

seconds.headline: Gold falls 3% to its lowest in over a year after hawkish Fed minutes, and Indian prices drop to ₹1,29,990
seconds.short: Spot gold fell 3.2% to $3,726.19 an ounce on Wednesday, its lowest since September 2025, after minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting showed officials expect more rate rises to control inflation. In India, 24-carat gold fell 3.1% to ₹1,29,990 for 10 grams, down from ₹1,62,154 at its August peak.

why.text: Gold has lost a fifth of its value in India in three months, a blow to households that hold much of their savings in it.

more: Higher rates raise the cost of holding gold, which pays no interest, and the dollar rose to a 19-month high. Fed governor Christopher Waller said the Fed should either raise rates by half a point in December or signal faster increases in 2027. Markets put a 7.3% chance on a half-point rise next month.

"Barring a quick reversal, today's damage suggests a probe of 3350-3450 in the coming weeks," said independent analyst Tai Wong. Silver fell 5% to $45.03 an ounce and platinum 4.1% to $1,370.70, both at their lowest since September 2025. Indian shares held up on Thursday, with the Sensex up 0.6% at 2pm.

stories.headline: Musk says he feels "pretty foolish" about spending $446m on the midterms, and that he is "not Maga"
stories.short: Elon Musk said he felt "pretty foolish" about the $446m he gave to back Republicans in this month's midterms, the most of any individual donor, after the party lost both houses of Congress. "I'm not Maga," he told the New York Times DealBook Summit. He added that Republican candidates would probably have done worse without the money.

why.text: It is a sharp turn for Trump's biggest backer, and Democrats in charge of Congress have promised closer scrutiny of tech companies, including Musk's.

more: "I'm not sure what Maga means," he said. "If that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don't have that." At a Trump rally in 2024 he had joked, "I'm not just Maga, I'm dark, gothic Maga." Much of his spending went to Texas, where many of his companies are based.

Musk led the Department of Government Efficiency early in Trump's second term, and in October the Pentagon named him co-lead of a study on the future of warfare called Project Meridian. In Georgia, where SpaceX runs data centres, the newly elected Democratic governor has promised to limit the spread of such centres.

stories.headline: GTA 6 launches with a score of 99 on Metacritic, 13 years after GTA 5, and Modi borrows its look for a post
stories.short: Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight on Thursday, with an aggregate score of 99 out of 100 on Metacritic from more than 150 reviews. IGN called it "the single most impressive video game I have ever played". Pre-orders passed 15.8 million copies, worth $1.54bn, by 17 November.

why.text: It is likely to be the most lucrative release in gaming history, and its launch has spilled into work, school and even Indian politics.

more: Rockstar Games spent an estimated more than $1bn making it, and delayed it twice from 2025. It follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a criminal couple, in Leonida and Vice City, stand-ins for Florida and Miami. It is the first new game in the series since GTA V in September 2013, and nearly one in five US workers plan to take time off to play.

"India is playing a whole new game," Narendra Modi posted on X, with graphics in the game's style comparing India now with 2013, when the UPA was in power. One showed extreme poverty falling from 27% to 2.6%, according to the World Bank, and others covered sanitation, solar capacity, data prices and defence exports.

update.new: The game is out to rave reviews.

stories.headline: NASA says Voyager 1 has become the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth
stories.short: Voyager 1 reached a light-day from Earth, the distance light travels in 24 hours, about 26 billion km, at 10:16 GMT on Wednesday, according to NASA's calculations. No other spacecraft has gone so far. Because a signal takes a day each way, engineers at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory must wait to confirm it.

why.text: A probe launched in 1977 is still sending science home from interstellar space, farther away than anything people have built.

more: "Reaching one light-day is an astounding feat, one that I never expected to see," said project manager Suzanne Dodd. Voyager 1 travels at almost 61,000 km/h. It left the heliosphere, the bubble of particles and magnetic fields around the sun, in 2012, and its twin Voyager 2 followed in 2018. NASA has scheduled an event on Thursday to discuss the milestone.

Recent power-saving steps could keep both probes in contact with Earth for three or four more years, a JPL spokesperson said. There is enough power to keep the current instruments running through the 50th anniversary of the launch next year, but beyond that is hard to predict for spacecraft nearly 50 years old.

stories.headline: Alcaraz beats Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 to reach the ATP Finals semi-finals, but plays with strapping on his hamstring
stories.short: Carlos Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 in 72 minutes in Turin on Wednesday for his 11th win in a row, and his place in the semi-finals was confirmed when Frances Tiafoe beat Flavio Cobolli. But he finished with heavy strapping on his upper left leg after feeling "a little problem" with his hamstring.

why.text: Alcaraz is the favourite for the one big title he has never won, so the state of his leg matters more than his last group match.

more: He was a set and a break up when he had treatment. "Right now I'm just feeling OK," he said. "We will see with my team and physio, but I think the rest of today and tomorrow are really going to be important days ahead of me." Asked what pleased him most, he said: "Everything."

He plays Cobolli, who cannot qualify after losing 7-6, 6-0 to Tiafoe, in his last group match on Friday at 18:30 IST. Since returning at the US Open in August after four months out with a wrist injury, Alcaraz has won three titles and lost twice in 24 matches. He lost last year's final in Turin to Jannik Sinner.
